title: Optimal performance in a chaotic Floquet quantum battery
abstract: We study a quantum battery consisting of $N$ qubits interacting uniformly with each other. Starting from its ground state, the battery is charged by introducing periodic kicks in the transverse direction along with adding disorder in the interaction direction. Although the battery Hamiltonian along with the initial state preserves the permutation symmetry, the dynamics in presence of disorder during the charging phase takes the system out of the permutation symmetric subspace, resulting to a larger amount of stored energy as compared to that without disorder. In the limit of large disorder, this interplay brings in a possibility of a chaotic charging phase when stored energy can be exactly calculated using random matrix theory. More importantly, we also find that the energy fluctuations decrease and become negligible in the limit of large disorder, which is also when the energy stored is maximum, a condition highly desirable for the optimum functioning of the battery. We complete the battery cycle by considering the storage phase in the presence of dephasing noise. We find that for larger disorder strengths, the ergotropy remains close to the stored energy, indicating nearly complete energy extractability with an efficiency approaching unity.
summary: This work analyzes the optimal operation of a quantum battery driven by periodic kicks and disorder. The key finding is that disorder drives the system into a chaotic regime, maximizing stored energy while simultaneously suppressing detrimental energy fluctuations. This suggests that controlled disorder can be a mechanism to enhance the stability and efficiency of quantum energy storage devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how introducing disorder during the charging phase of a quantum battery affects its stored energy, energy fluctuations, and ultimately its extractable work.
main_result: Optimal battery performance (maximal energy storage with suppressed fluctuations) is achieved in the chaotic, permutation-symmetry-broken regime, where dynamics explore the full Hilbert space.
method: The analysis combines Floquet theory for periodic driving, Random Matrix Theory (RMT) for large disorder limits, and the Lindblad master equation for open system dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum battery of N interacting qubits, modeled by an all-to-all interacting spin chain Hamiltonian. Charging is achieved via a periodically driven Floquet protocol, and storage/extraction is analyzed under pure dephasing noise.
key_observables: Stored energy, energy fluctuations (variance), Ergotropy (extractable work), and the chaoticity parameter.
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($w$), number of qubits ($N$), and the driving frequency/kicks ($k$).
main_assumptions: The system starts in the ground state, and the analysis often compares results between the Permutation Symmetric Subspace (PSS) and the Full Hilbert Space (FHS).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the battery cycle (Charging $	o$ Storage $	o$ Extraction) showing energy partitioning, and plots track the evolution of average stored energy, energy variance, and charging power as a function of kicks/time.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the battery cycle: first, the charging phase where disorder is introduced; second, the storage phase modeled with dephasing noise; and third, the extraction capability quantified by ergotropy.
why_interesting: It bridges concepts from quantum chaos (Floquet systems, disorder) and quantum thermodynamics (quantum batteries), providing quantitative metrics (RMT benchmarks) for optimizing energy storage and retrieval efficiency.
